(no insurer may transact insurance without a subsisting Certificate of Authority) read together with the current NAIC UCAA Expansion Application instructions and the target state's admission checklist, re-read at each market-entry decision; supporting Arkansas, Arizona and California admission requirements checked the same way

In-scope processes.value: Market-entry approval (new state, new writing company, or new line of authority) up to the CoA scope gate that must clear before any quote, bind, producer appointment or CE-bearing solicitation occurs in that state - all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: NAIC iSite+ / State Based Systems company record showing CoA lines of authority by NAIC co-code; CoA certificates and UCAA packets held in the compliance evidence repository

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per market entry - the CoA must be issued before the first policy effective date; UCAA Expansion review typically runs 60-90 days plus deficiency cycles, and each state's annual CoA continuation fee falls on its own date (commonly 1 March or 1 July)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Market-entry tracker milestone alerts at T-180 / T-120 / T-60 days before the target first-writing date, plus annual continuation-fee reminders 45 days ahead of each state's due date

checklist.step: Open a market-entry request and capture exactly what will be written
actions: Open the market-entry queue and raise a request record with the target state, target first-writing date and the sponsoring business unit.
Ask the Head of Distribution for the writing company that will carry the business and record its NAIC co-code and FEIN on the request.
List each product to be sold with its NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix TOI/Sub-TOI, and mark whether it is personal lines, commercial lines, life, annuity or accident & health.
Record whether the company will write on an admitted basis or through a surplus lines placement, because a surplus lines route needs an eligibility listing rather than a CoA.
checklist.done: the request record names the state, the writing company co-code, the target first-writing date and every product with its TOI/Sub-TOI.

checklist.step: Pull the subsisting Certificate of Authority for each writing company
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the Company Demographics / State Licensing screen for the co-code on the request.
Export the state-by-state licence record showing each jurisdiction and the lines of authority granted, with the original admission date and current status.
Pull the paper or PDF CoA certificate for the target state from the compliance evidence repository and compare the printed lines of authority to the iSite+ record.
Where iSite+ and the certificate disagree, email the domiciliary regulator's company licensing analyst for the authoritative version and log the reply on the request.
checklist.done: a dated iSite+ export and the matching CoA certificate are attached to the request for every writing company named.

checklist.step: Map each requested product to the target state's own line-of-authority wording
actions: Open the target state's insurance code section listing the kinds of insurance (for Alabama, Ala. Code sec. 27-5-2 through 27-5-9) and copy the exact statutory line names.
Against each requested TOI/Sub-TOI write the state's line name that authorises it - for example Casualty, Property, Marine, Life, Disability, Surety, Vehicle.
Flag hybrid products that need two lines (e.g. a package policy needing both Property and Casualty, or an annuity rider needing Life plus Disability for LTC benefits).
Have the Insurance Product Manager confirm in writing that the product list is final for launch and note the confirmation date.
checklist.done: every requested product carries the target state's statutory line-of-authority name, with hybrids showing both required lines.

checklist.step: Compare the requested grid to the granted grid and list the authority gaps
actions: Build a state/line matrix with one row per writing company and one column per statutory line, filled from the iSite+ export.
Overlay the requested products and mark each cell GRANTED, GAP or NOT REQUIRED.
For each GAP record whether it is a new-state admission (no CoA at all) or a line addition to an existing CoA, because the two take different applications.
Circulate the matrix to Regulatory Counsel and the sponsoring underwriting leader and record their acknowledgement date.
checklist.done: the matrix shows a GRANTED / GAP / NOT REQUIRED status for every requested product-state-company cell, with each gap typed.

checklist.step: Test the financial admission thresholds the state will apply
actions: Read the target state's minimum paid-in capital and surplus requirement for each line to be added, and the higher of the state's figure or the domiciliary figure that will actually apply.
Pull capital and surplus from the most recent filed Annual Statement, Page 3 (Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds), and compare it to the requirement line by line.

Check the UCAA seasoning expectation - the Expansion Application generally assumes at least 3 years of operating history and 3 years of audited statements - and note any waiver that must be requested.
Compute the RBC ratio from the latest RBC filing and confirm it clears the state's stated comfort level; escalate to the Chief Financial Officer if it does not.
checklist.done: capital, surplus, seasoning and RBC are each tested against the state's stated threshold with the tested value written on the request.

checklist.step: Choose the admission route and get counsel to fix it in writing
actions: Decide between the UCAA Primary Application (redomestication), the UCAA Expansion Application (new state for a seasoned insurer) and the UCAA Corporate Amendments Application (adding a line to an existing CoA).
Confirm the target state accepts UCAA for the chosen route by reading its entry in the UCAA state-specific requirements pages; some states add their own forms on top.
Where the launch cannot wait for admission, opine in writing on the fronting or surplus lines alternative and its own eligibility conditions.
Record the chosen route, the citation relied on and counsel's name and date on the request record.
checklist.done: the request names one admission route, the state pages that support it and a dated counsel opinion.

checklist.step: Assemble the UCAA application packet
actions: Download the current UCAA application form set and the target state's UCAA state-specific requirements checklist from the NAIC UCAA pages.

Assemble the core exhibits: Certificate of Compliance and Certificate of Deposit from the domiciliary regulator (both dated within the state's freshness window, usually 30-60 days), certified Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws, the last 3 years of audited GAAP or statutory financials, the latest Annual and Quarterly Statements, the plan of operation with 3-year pro forma projections by line, and the Holding Company Form B registration.
Request from Product Development the form and rate filings the state expects at or shortly after admission, and note that they file through SERFF separately.
Confirm the filing fee amount and payment method on the state's checklist and raise the payment request with Finance.
Run the state's checklist line by line and mark each item attached, requested or not applicable with a reason.
checklist.done: every line of the state's UCAA checklist is marked attached, requested with a due date, or not applicable with a written reason.

checklist.step: Order biographical affidavits and third-party verifications for officers and directors
actions: List every officer, director and key functional manager the state requires an NAIC Biographical Affidavit (Form 11) for.
Issue the affidavit to each individual through the e-signature workflow and require the notarised signature page.
Engage an NAIC-accepted third-party verification vendor for each affidavit and track the report to completion, since most states will not accept an affidavit older than 3 years or an unverified one.
Escalate any disclosed criminal, regulatory or bankruptcy matter to Regulatory Counsel before the packet goes out.
checklist.done: each required individual has a notarised, in-date biographical affidavit with a completed third-party verification report attached.

checklist.step: Post the statutory deposit and appoint the agent for service of process
actions: Read the target state's deposit requirement (amount, eligible securities and whether it is held by the state treasurer or a custodian under a joint-custody agreement).
Instruct the custodian to move the securities and obtain the deposit receipt or trust certificate the state will accept as proof.
Complete the appointment of the Commissioner of Insurance (or the state's registered agent form) as attorney for service of process and have it executed by an authorised officer.
File the executed appointment and the deposit receipt into the UCAA packet and note the amounts on the request record.
checklist.done: a deposit receipt for the required amount and an executed service-of-process appointment are in the packet.

checklist.step: Submit the application and work every deficiency letter to closure
actions: Submit the packet by the channel the state's UCAA page specifies (electronic UCAA submission, state portal upload, or courier of the paper set) and capture the submission receipt and date.
Open a tracker issue per submission and set the expected review window from the state's stated turnaround.
Log each deficiency letter with its date, the items raised and a named owner, and answer inside the state's response window - commonly 30 days before the file is closed for inactivity.
Keep a running contact log of every call and email with the state's company licensing analyst, with names and dates.
checklist.done: the submission receipt is on file and every deficiency item has a dated response and a closure note from the state.

checklist.step: Record the issued Certificate of Authority and refresh the authority matrix
actions: Save the issued CoA certificate under the writing company and state, naming it <co-code>-<state>-CoA-<issue date>.
Re-pull the iSite+ state licensing record and confirm the new state or line now shows as active with the expected lines of authority.
Update the authority matrix cells from GAP to GRANTED with the CoA issue date and the granted line names.
Publish the refreshed matrix to Underwriting, Distribution and Producer Licensing so appointments can be planned against it.
checklist.done: the CoA is filed, iSite+ confirms the grant, and the published matrix shows the state/line as GRANTED with its issue date.

checklist.step: Configure the writing block so the state/line cannot be bound before the CoA date
actions: In the policy administration product-availability table, set the state/line row's earliest effective date to the CoA issue date for that writing company.
Turn on the hard-stop validation so a quote or bind attempt in an unauthorised state/line is rejected rather than warned.
Ask the Configuration Engineer to run a bind test in the pre-production environment one day before and one day after the CoA date and keep both screenshots.
Mirror the same date control in the rating and underwriting workstation so a manual override cannot bypass it.
checklist.done: a pre-production test shows binding rejected the day before the CoA date and accepted on it, with both screenshots retained.

checklist.step: Release the market-entry gate and tell the field the earliest bind date
actions: Review the authority matrix, the CoA certificate and the pre-production bind test before signing the gate release.
Publish the per-state, per-line earliest bind date to underwriting and to the Agency Relations Manager for onward distribution.
State plainly in the release that producer appointments and solicitation may not start before that date, and hand the date to Producer Licensing.
Record the gate release with your name and date on the market-entry request.
checklist.done: a signed gate release carries the earliest bind date per state and line and has been sent to underwriting and distribution.

checklist.step: Calendar the annual continuation, fees and premium tax registration
actions: Read the state's CoA continuation requirement (annual renewal fee, annual statement filing and any officer certification) and its due date.
Register the writing company for premium tax and any surplus lines, fire marshal or guaranty fund assessments the state levies on the new lines.
Load the continuation due date and the premium tax due dates into the regulatory calendar with reminders 45 days ahead.
Name the accountable preparer and reviewer for each recurring obligation.
checklist.done: continuation, premium tax and assessment dates are on the regulatory calendar with owners and 45-day reminders.

checklist.step: File the admission evidence and apply the retention label
actions: Move the full admission folder - request record, authority matrix, UCAA packet, affidavits and verifications, deposit receipt, deficiency correspondence and CoA - into the repository under the writing company and state.
Apply the retention label of 10 years from withdrawal so the record survives any future exit from the state.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by co-code, state, line of authority and CoA issue date.
Hand the folder reference to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the examiner-response pack.
checklist.done: the admission folder is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by co-code, state and line.

testing.step: Build the population of activations and newly written state/line business
actions: Extract every policy with a first effective date inside the quarter, grouped by writing company co-code, state and statutory line.
Extract the market-entry request log for the quarter and list every state/line activated or released.
Add manual and legacy-system bindings so business written outside the main policy admin platform cannot escape the population.
Reconcile the policy count to the quarter's written premium register and clear the difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the written premium register and the extractor has signed it as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the internal CoA inventory to the regulator's own record
actions: Pull a fresh iSite+ state licensing export for every writing company as at quarter end.
Match it line by line to the published authority matrix on co-code + state + line of authority.
List every cell the matrix shows as GRANTED that iSite+ does not, and every line iSite+ shows that the matrix omits.
Treat any unmatched GRANTED cell as an automatic exception, since it is the cell underwriting relied on.
testing.done: the authority matrix is reconciled cell by cell to iSite+ and every break is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of state/line activations completed in the quarter.
Take 25 policies at random using a recorded seed from states entered in the last 12 months, with a floor of 40 items overall.
Force in every hybrid product identified as needing two lines of authority.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all activations and hybrid-line products.

testing.step: Re-perform the line-of-authority mapping independently
actions: For each sampled product read the state's statutory list of kinds of insurance and reach your own line-of-authority conclusion before opening the matrix.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded mapping; a right answer with the wrong statutory line is still an exception.
Check hybrid products carry every line their benefits require, not just the dominant one.
Capture the statute page you relied on into the workpaper with the date read.
testing.done: each sampled product has an independent mapping note and a captured statutory source.

testing.step: Trace each sampled policy to a CoA that pre-dates its effective date
actions: Open the CoA certificate for the sampled policy's writing company and state and read the issue date and granted lines.
Confirm the CoA issue date is earlier than the policy effective date and that the policy's line appears on the certificate.
Where the line was added later, confirm the Corporate Amendments approval date also pre-dates the policy.
List any policy without a pre-dating CoA as an unauthorised-writing breach rather than a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled policy traces to a CoA issued before its effective date and covering its line.

testing.step: Test the UCAA packet completeness and deficiency closure on sampled activations
actions: Open the state's UCAA state-specific checklist as it stood on the submission date and walk it against the filed packet.
Confirm the Certificate of Compliance and Certificate of Deposit were within the state's freshness window at submission.
Confirm every officer and director had a notarised biographical affidavit with a completed third-party verification.
Read each deficiency letter and confirm a dated response exists inside the state's response window and the state closed the item.
testing.done: each sampled activation shows a complete checklist walk and a closed response for every deficiency raised.

testing.step: Recompute the financial thresholds and the admission lead time
actions: Recompute capital and surplus from the filed Annual Statement Page 3 and compare to the state's minimum for each granted line.
Recompute the RBC ratio from the filed RBC exhibit and compare to the threshold recorded on the request.
Recompute elapsed days from submission receipt to CoA issue and compare to the T-180/T-120/T-60 plan to see whether the plan was realistic or the launch date was simply moved.
Note any activation where the target first-writing date was met only because the gate was released early.
testing.done: capital, surplus, RBC and lead-time figures are independently recomputed and agreed or listed as differences.

testing.step: Prove the system writing block actually held
actions: Read the product-availability configuration history for each sampled state/line and confirm the earliest effective date equals the CoA issue date.
Pull the platform's override and exception report and list every bind that bypassed the state/line validation, with the user id and reason.
Attempt a controlled bind in the pre-production environment for one state/line not on the CoA and confirm it is rejected.
Screenshot the configuration history and the rejection into the workpaper.
testing.done: configuration history matches the CoA dates, all overrides are listed with a user and reason, and the rejection test is captured.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying the co-code, state, line, policy count and premium at risk.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: gate released early, matrix stale, product mapped to the wrong line, override used, or activation never requested.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for unauthorised writing open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering rescission, assumption reinsurance or state-directed cure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Compute the exception rate and the premium bound outside authority, and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who prepared no sampled UCAA filing or determination, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any unauthorised-writing breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with an exception rate, premium at risk, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Take in the contracting request and open a verification record
actions: Open the onboarding queue and pick up requests with status 'Contracting submitted' from the Agency Relations Manager.
Create a verification record holding legal name, date of birth, National Producer Number (NPN), FEIN or SSN reference, resident state, and the agency or hierarchy the producer will write under.
Record from the request which states the producer will solicit in and which products they will sell, since that is what the licence must cover.
Reject and return any request with no NPN or with a name that does not match the government identification supplied, rather than searching on a guess.
checklist.done: a verification record exists with a confirmed NPN, resident state, target states and target products.

checklist.step: Pull the NIPR Producer Database report
actions: Sign in to the NIPR Gateway with the company's PDB subscription credentials.
Open PDB Reports and run a Producer Report by NPN; use the name and date-of-birth search only to establish the NPN when it is genuinely unknown, then re-run by NPN.
Order the report with regulatory actions and appointment history included, not the abbreviated status-only view.
Save the report as a dated PDF named <NPN>-PDB-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and attach it to the verification record - this is the evidence behind the whole gate.
checklist.done: a dated PDB report PDF including regulatory actions and appointments is attached to the verification record.

checklist.step: Test the resident licence status, class and expiry
actions: On the PDB report read the resident state licence: licence class (Producer, Limited Lines, Adjuster), status, original issue date and expiration date.
Reject any status other than Active - Inactive, Expired, Suspended, Revoked, Voluntarily Surrendered and Pending all stop the gate.
Where the expiration date falls inside the next 60 days, hand the record to the renewal desk before releasing the gate so the producer does not lapse mid-onboarding.
Write the resident status, class and expiry onto the verification record with the date read.
checklist.done: the resident licence is confirmed Active with its class and expiry recorded, or the record is stopped.

checklist.step: Test a non-resident licence for every state the producer will solicit in
actions: List every target state from the verification record and find each one on the PDB report's licence section.
For each, record licence type (non-resident producer), status, lines of authority and expiry.
Mark any target state with no licence as a gap and route it to the non-resident licence application step - never assume reciprocity has already been exercised.
Check the home-state reciprocity condition: a non-resident licence dies with the resident licence, so flag any producer whose resident licence is not clean.
checklist.done: every target state shows an active non-resident licence on the PDB report or is marked as a gap to be applied for.

checklist.step: Match the lines of authority to the products the producer will actually sell
actions: Build a match sheet with one row per target state and one column per product to be sold.
Fill each cell with the PDB line of authority that authorises the product - Life, Accident & Health or Sickness, Property, Casualty, Personal Lines, Variable Life and Variable Annuity, Surplus Lines.
Flag the traps: an annuity needs the Life line in most states, an LTC rider needs Accident & Health, and variable products need both the Variable line and FINRA registration.
Where a product has no authorising line in a state, remove the product from that producer's writing scope in the agency/producer management system rather than relying on the producer to self-police.
checklist.done: every product-state cell shows an authorising line of authority held by the producer, or the product is removed from scope.

checklist.step: Verify the business entity licence and its designated responsible licensed producer
actions: Run a PDB Business Entity report on the agency's entity NPN or FEIN for every state the agency will operate in.
Confirm the entity licence is active and its lines of authority cover the products, and confirm the entity's legal name matches the name on the producer agreement and the commission payee record.

Read the designated responsible licensed producer (DRLP) named for each state and confirm that individual holds an active licence with matching lines - a lapsed DRLP invalidates the entity's authority in that state.
Where the agency writes under a DBA, confirm the assumed name is registered with the state insurance department as well as with the secretary of state.
checklist.done: the entity licence, its lines, its registered name and an active DRLP are confirmed for every state the agency operates in.

checklist.step: Review regulatory actions and disclosures on the PDB report
actions: Read the Regulatory Actions section of the PDB report, which surfaces state actions reported to the NAIC Regulatory Information Retrieval System.
For each action record the state, action date, type (fine, suspension, revocation, cease and desist, licence denial) and the underlying conduct.
Order the underlying consent order or state order from the acting department when the conduct involves misappropriation, forgery, rebating or unlicensed activity.
Escalate any action involving dishonesty or breach of trust to the 18 U.S.C. sec. 1033 screening owner before the gate is released.
checklist.done: every regulatory action on the PDB report is documented with its order and either cleared or escalated to 1033 screening.

checklist.step: Confirm securities registration where variable or registered products are in scope
actions: For any producer selling variable annuities, variable life or registered index-linked annuities, look the individual up on FINRA BrokerCheck by CRD number.
Confirm the Series 6 or Series 7 and Series 63 registrations are current and that the producer is registered with a broker-dealer that holds a selling agreement with the company.
Confirm the state variable line of authority is on the PDB report as well - the FINRA registration alone does not authorise the state solicitation.
Record the CRD number, broker-dealer name and selling agreement reference on the verification record.
checklist.done: CRD registration, broker-dealer selling agreement and the state variable line are all confirmed for variable-product producers.

checklist.step: Confirm product training is complete before the appointment is transmitted
actions: Check the producer's training record for the state-mandated pre-sale training the product requires: the 4-hour annuity best interest training under the NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions model, the 8-hour initial long-term care training plus the 4-hour refresher due every 24 months, and the 3-hour NFIP flood course for flood business.
Confirm the company's own product-specific training for the exact contract series the producer will sell has been completed and dated.
Where training is outstanding, assign the course with a due date before the planned appointment date and hold the gate.
Export the completion certificates with dates and attach them to the verification record.
checklist.done: every state-mandated and product-specific training requirement shows a dated completion certificate on the record.

checklist.step: Write the verified profile and release the solicitation flag
actions: Enter into the producer record: NPN, per-state licence status, lines of authority, expiry dates, entity NPN, DRLP and the products approved for sale.
Set the solicitation flag to Approved with the effective date equal to today, never backdated to the contract date.
Set the per-state writing scope so the record itself, not a manual instruction, controls what the producer can submit.
Attach the PDB PDF, the match sheet and the training certificates to the producer record before saving.
checklist.done: the producer record carries a verified per-state, per-line writing scope with the solicitation flag dated today and evidence attached.

checklist.step: Hold new business and commission payment behind the flag
actions: Confirm the commission system reads the solicitation flag and the per-state scope from the producer record rather than a local copy.
Set the payee record to suspend commission on any policy whose writing NPN is not Approved for that state and line on the application signed date.
Ask the Production Support Analyst for the daily reject report of held commissions and work it within two business days.
Confirm new business intake rejects an application whose writing NPN fails the same test, so the block is preventive rather than a payment-time catch.
checklist.done: both new business intake and commission payment reject an unapproved writing NPN, evidenced by a dated reject report.

checklist.step: Apply for the missing non-resident licences through NIPR
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Non-Resident Licensing and start an application for each gap state under the producer's NPN.
Select the lines of authority that mirror the resident licence, since reciprocity grants only what the home state already gave.
Pay the state licence fee plus the NIPR transaction fee and capture the confirmation number and submission date.
Track the application to issue and re-pull the PDB report to confirm the new state appears active before the writing scope is widened.
checklist.done: each gap state has a submitted NIPR application with a confirmation number and a PDB re-pull confirming issue.

checklist.step: Publish the approved writing scope to the producer and the field
actions: Send the producer a scope letter listing the states, lines and products they are approved to solicit and the effective date.
State in the letter that solicitation outside that scope is a contract breach and will trigger commission clawback.
Publish the same scope on the producer's portal profile so the field can see it without calling Licensing.
Copy the Territory Manager so the field leader is accountable for the boundary.
checklist.done: the producer and their field leader have a dated scope letter and the same scope is visible on the portal profile.

checklist.step: Subscribe the NPN to continuous status monitoring
actions: Add the NPN to the company's NIPR Alerts subscription so licence status changes, new regulatory actions and expirations push daily.
Route the daily alert file into the licensing work queue with an automatic case for any status leaving Active.
Set the rule that a non-Active status suspends the solicitation flag the same business day, before any human review.
Test the rule quarterly with a known lapsed NPN and keep the screenshot.
checklist.done: the NPN is on the daily alert subscription and a non-Active status demonstrably suspends the flag the same day.

checklist.step: File the verification evidence and apply retention
actions: Move the verification folder - PDB report, match sheet, entity and DRLP evidence, training certificates, scope letter - into the repository under the producer NPN.
Apply the retention label of 5 years after the producer relationship ends, matching the market conduct record retention expectation.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, agency entity NPN, state and verification date.
Hand the index reference to Market Conduct so it can be pulled straight into an exam response.
checklist.done: the verification folder is filed under the NPN, labelled for 5-year retention and searchable by NPN, entity and state.

testing.step: Build the population of new appointments and new business applications
actions: Extract every producer contracted or appointed in the quarter with NPN, states, lines and solicitation flag effective date.
Extract every new business application received in the quarter with its writing producer NPN, signed date, state and product.
Add applications taken through the digital self-service and portal channels so producer-assisted digital sales are in scope.
Reconcile the application count to the new business register and clear the difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the new business register and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Re-pull PDB independently and reconcile it to the roster
actions: Run a fresh PDB extract for every NPN in the population using the auditor's own PDB access, not a copy supplied by Licensing.
Match on NPN and compare licence status, lines of authority and expiry against the producer record's stored scope.
List every producer whose stored scope is wider than PDB supports as an automatic exception.
Note any NPN that does not resolve in PDB at all, which usually means the NPN was mistyped at onboarding.
testing.done: every roster NPN is reconciled to a fresh PDB pull and all scope-wider-than-PDB cases are listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across both populations
actions: Take 100% of producers appointed with a non-resident licence issued in the same month as their first application.
Take 40 applications at random with a recorded seed, stratified so each product family and at least 10 states are represented.
Force in every application written by a producer carrying a regulatory action on PDB.
Record the seed, strata, population size and draw date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, stratified by product and state, and includes all producers with regulatory actions.

testing.step: Re-perform the licence check as at the application signed date
actions: For each sampled application read the PDB licence history and establish the licence status in that state on the application signed date, not today.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the producer could lawfully solicit that product in that state on that date before opening the verification record.
Compare to the recorded verification; a licence that was pending, expired or in another state's name on the signed date is a fail.
Capture the PDB licence-history screen into the workpaper with the date read.
testing.done: each sampled application has an independent as-at-signed-date licence conclusion with a captured PDB screen.

testing.step: Test the line-of-authority to product match on the sample
actions: For each sampled application map the product sold to the line of authority the state requires, working from the state's licence class definitions.
Compare to the lines PDB shows the producer held on the signed date.
Pay particular attention to annuities sold on a Property/Casualty-only licence and LTC riders sold without Accident & Health.
List every mismatch as a fail even where the producer held some other active licence in the state.
testing.done: every sampled product is matched to a line the producer actually held on the signed date, or the mismatch is listed.

testing.step: Test the business entity and DRLP position behind agency-written business
actions: For each sampled agency-written application pull the entity PDB report and confirm the entity licence was active in that state on the signed date.
Confirm the DRLP named for that state held an active individual licence with matching lines on the same date.
Confirm the commission payee legal name matches the licensed entity name exactly, including any registered DBA.
Flag any payment made to an entity licensed in a different state or under an unregistered trade name.
testing.done: each agency-written sample item shows an active entity licence, a licensed DRLP and a matching payee name on the signed date.

testing.step: Test that the training prerequisites pre-dated the first sale
actions: For sampled annuity, LTC and flood applications pull the producer's training completion certificates from the learning management system.
Confirm the 4-hour annuity best interest completion, the 8-hour LTC initial or the in-date 4-hour LTC refresher, and the 3-hour NFIP course as the product requires.
Recompute the LTC refresher due date as completion date plus 24 months and confirm the sale fell inside it.
List sales made before the completion date as fails, not as documentation gaps.
testing.done: every training-gated sample item shows a completion date earlier than the sale and an in-date refresher where required.

testing.step: Prove the preventive controls blocked unapproved writing NPNs
actions: Pull the new business intake reject log and the commission hold report for the quarter and count rejections triggered by the solicitation flag.
Trace 10 rejected items through to their resolution and confirm none was released without a fresh PDB pull.
Pull the override log and list every user who released a hold, with the reason given.
Run a controlled test with a deliberately unapproved NPN in the non-production environment and screenshot the rejection.
testing.done: reject and override logs are analysed, ten rejections are traced to resolution, and the controlled test rejection is captured.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, state, product, application count, premium and commission paid.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: verification skipped, stale PDB, wrong line mapped, flag backdated, alert not actioned, or entity/DRLP lapse.
Set an owner and a remediation date and decide with Regulatory Counsel whether commissions must be clawed back and whether the state requires a self-report of unlicensed production.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, commission decision and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Compute the unlicensed-production count and the documentation defect rate and compare them to the zero-tolerance and 2% thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have an independent reviewer outside Licensing Ops, who performed no sampled verification, sign the workpaper.
Report the results and any unlicensed production to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with both rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Ala. Code sec. 27-7-30 and sec. 27-7-30.2 (appointment filing and notice of termination for cause within 30 days, with a copy to the producer within 15 days of notifying the Commissioner), read with the ALDOI appointment bulletins; Arkansas, Arizona and California windows read separately because the day counts differ by state

In-scope processes.value: Appointment transmission triggered by contract execution or first application, just-in-time appointment states triggered at first policy issue, and termination transmission triggered by resignation, non-renewal, for-cause action or death - all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway Appointment / Termination transactions and the resulting PDB appointment record; triggers and day counts held in the agency/producer management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Appointment and Termination Procedure - trigger capture, per-state day-count table, NIPR transmission, reject rework, for-cause statement drafting, producer notice, and system access and commission shut-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; the per-state day-count table is re-verified against state statutes annually and on any appointment bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven - appointment filed within the state's window (commonly 15 days from contract execution or first application, whichever is earlier); termination notice within 30 days of the termination effective date, and the copy to the producer within 15 days of notifying the Commissioner

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case ageing alerts at day 5 and day 10 of an open appointment trigger and at day 10 and day 20 of an open termination, with automatic escalation to the Producer Compliance Manager at day 12 and day 25

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every appointment or termination transmitted after the statutory window is logged with the days late, the state's late-filing penalty exposure and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late filing and every for-cause termination package before it is transmitted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All appointment triggers and all termination events in the quarter, by producer NPN, writing company and state, taken from the contract log, the first-application log and the HR/distribution separation feed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed for-cause notices and on terminations never filed; late filings tolerated to 3% of the population before the control is rated ineffective, with any filing more than 30 days late escalated individually

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have transmitted or approved any sampled appointment or termination

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly appointment and termination test workpaper (event population, NIPR confirmations, day-count recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: NIPR transaction confirmations, the PDB appointment history and the for-cause statements with proof of producer notice, producible for an appointment data call within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state appointment inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any for-cause statement content and any response touching a producer's own regulatory record

checklist.step: Capture the appointment trigger the moment it happens
actions: Subscribe the licensing queue to two events: producer agreement executed (from the contracting workflow) and first application received (from new business intake).
For each event open an appointment case holding NPN, writing company co-code, state, trigger type and trigger date.
Where both events exist, set the trigger date to the earlier of the two, because most statutes run the clock from whichever comes first.
Reject a trigger with no state or no co-code back to the Agency Relations Manager the same day rather than guessing the writing company.
checklist.done: every appointment case shows NPN, co-code, state, trigger type and the earlier of contract and first-application dates.

checklist.step: Compute the statutory appointment deadline from the per-state table
actions: Open the maintained per-state appointment table and read the window for the case's state - typically 15 days from the trigger, with some states allowing 30 and some requiring the appointment before any solicitation.
Compute deadline = trigger date + window days and record it on the case, noting whether the state counts calendar or business days.
Mark the case JIT where the state operates just-in-time appointment, so the obligation attaches at first policy issue instead.
Where the table has no verified entry for the state, stop and get the Producer Compliance Manager to source the statute before transmitting.
checklist.done: each case carries a computed statutory deadline, the day-count basis and a JIT flag where applicable.

checklist.step: Confirm the licence prerequisites before transmitting the appointment
actions: Re-pull the PDB report for the NPN and confirm an active licence in the appointment state with the lines the appointment will carry.
Confirm the writing company holds a subsisting Certificate of Authority for that state and line by checking the published authority matrix.
Confirm any state-mandated pre-appointment training and the 18 U.S.C. sec. 1033 screening disposition are complete.
Hold the case, and tell the Agency Relations Manager in writing, where any prerequisite fails - an appointment transmitted for an unlicensed producer will simply reject and burn the clock.
checklist.done: an active licence, a covering CoA and completed screening and training are confirmed on the case before transmission.

checklist.step: Transmit the appointment through NIPR Gateway
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments and start a new appointment transaction for the company's co-code.

Enter the producer NPN, the state, the appointment type and the lines of authority to be appointed, and set the appointment effective date to the trigger date where the state permits backdating to it.
Submit and pay the state appointment fee plus the NIPR transaction fee, then capture the transaction confirmation number and submission timestamp.
Paste the confirmation number and timestamp onto the appointment case and attach the confirmation PDF.
checklist.done: the appointment is submitted with a captured NIPR confirmation number and timestamp attached to the case.

checklist.step: Work the NIPR reject and pending file to closure
actions: Download the daily NIPR transaction response file and list every rejected or pending appointment with its reason code.
Fix the common causes at source: NPN not licensed in the state, line not held, insufficient funds on the NIPR account, or company not authorised for the line.
Re-transmit inside the original statutory deadline wherever the days remain, and flag to the Producer Compliance Manager where they do not.
Confirm on PDB that the appointment now shows active for the state and co-code before closing the case.
checklist.done: no appointment case closes until PDB shows the appointment active, or it is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Handle the just-in-time appointment states separately
actions: Maintain the list of states that allow appointment at or after first policy issue rather than at contracting, and the days allowed after issue.
Set the policy administration feed to raise an appointment trigger the day a first policy issues for a producer with no appointment in that state.
Confirm the producer was licensed on the application signed date even though the appointment follows, because JIT relaxes appointment timing, not licensing.
Reconcile the JIT trigger list to the issued-policy list weekly so no first issue slips past the allowed window.
checklist.done: JIT states have a maintained window list, an issue-driven trigger and a weekly reconciliation with no unactioned first issues.

checklist.step: Capture the termination trigger from every source that can create one
actions: Feed the licensing queue from all five sources: producer resignation, company non-renewal of the agreement, for-cause action from Compliance or SIU, employment separation from HRIS, and notification of death.
Record on each termination case the NPN, affected states and co-codes, the termination effective date and the source of the trigger.
Confirm the affected-state list from the PDB appointment record rather than from the contract, because appointments often exist in states the contract no longer mentions.
Route the case to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day where the source is Compliance or SIU.
checklist.done: each termination case lists every appointed state from PDB, the effective date and the trigger source.

checklist.step: Classify the termination cause and decide the reporting basis
actions: Classify the termination as for cause or not for cause using the statutory grounds - misappropriation of premium, forgery, misrepresentation, fraud, unlicensed activity, or conduct that would support licence action.
Where the answer is arguable, write the facts and the reasoning on the case and send it to Regulatory Counsel rather than defaulting to not for cause.
Record that some states require the reason to be stated for every termination, so the classification drives the content of the filing, not whether one is made.
Set the case's statutory deadline as termination effective date plus the state's window, commonly 30 days.
checklist.done: the termination is classified with written reasoning, counsel is engaged on arguable cases, and the deadline is computed.

checklist.step: Draft the for-cause termination statement and get counsel approval
actions: Draft the statement of the facts and circumstances the state requires with the for-cause notice, keeping it to observed facts, dates, policy numbers and amounts.
Confirm the statement is supported by the SIU or Compliance investigation file and remove any conclusion the file does not evidence.
Brief the business on the qualified immunity that attaches to a good-faith report so the statement is not softened for fear of a defamation claim.
Approve the final statement in writing with your name and date on the termination case.
checklist.done: a fact-based, evidence-supported statement carries a dated counsel approval before it is transmitted.

checklist.step: Transmit the termination through NIPR inside the statutory window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the Termination transaction for the company co-code and enter the NPN, each affected state and the termination effective date.

Select the termination reason code the state offers and attach or upload the for-cause statement where the state accepts it electronically; where it does not, send the statement by the state's stated channel the same day.
Submit, capture the confirmation number and timestamp, and recompute days elapsed from the termination effective date to prove the window was met.
Confirm on PDB that the appointment now shows terminated with the correct date and reason before closing the case.
checklist.done: the termination shows on PDB with the right date and reason, and the elapsed day count is inside the state's window.

checklist.step: Send the producer their copy of the filed notice within 15 days
actions: Prepare the producer's copy of the notification filed with the Commissioner, including the statement where one was filed.
Send it to the producer's last known address of record on PDB by a method that evidences delivery, and calculate the deadline as 15 days from the date the Commissioner was notified.
File the delivery proof - tracking record or signed receipt - against the termination case.
Log any returned or undeliverable notice and re-send to the address held in the agency/producer management system.
checklist.done: the producer copy is sent within 15 days of the Commissioner notice with delivery proof on the case.

checklist.step: Shut off writing rights, system access and commission on the effective date
actions: Set the producer record's solicitation flag to Terminated with the effective date so new business intake rejects any further submission under that NPN.
Ask the Access Management Analyst to revoke agent portal, quoting and policy-view access on the effective date.
Set commission handling per the agreement - stop new commission, decide on renewal or trail commission and on any advance balance recovery - and record the decision.
Confirm the following day that no application was accepted and no commission paid under the NPN after the effective date.
checklist.done: writing rights, portal access and commission are all shut off on the effective date with next-day confirmation.

checklist.step: Reassign the orphaned book so policyholders keep a servicing producer
actions: Extract the terminated producer's in-force book by state, line and policy count.
Assign each policy to a receiving producer who is licensed and appointed in that state and line, and record the assignment date.
Send policyholders the servicing-change notice the state requires, within its stated timeframe.
Confirm renewal commission routing follows the assignment so no commission continues to flow to a terminated NPN by default.
checklist.done: every in-force policy has a licensed, appointed servicing producer and the policyholder notice has been sent.

checklist.step: Record both events in the appointment and termination register
actions: Write one register row per event with NPN, co-code, state, event type, trigger date, statutory deadline, transmission date, days elapsed and NIPR confirmation number.
Set a Late flag automatically where transmission date exceeds the deadline, rather than leaving it to judgement.
Link each row to the case folder holding the NIPR confirmation, the statement and the delivery proof.
Publish the ageing of open cases to the Producer Compliance Manager weekly.
checklist.done: the register holds one complete, source-linked row per event with an automatic late flag and a weekly ageing report.

checklist.step: File the transaction evidence and apply retention
actions: Move each case folder - trigger evidence, NIPR confirmations, PDB before-and-after captures, for-cause statement and counsel approval, producer notice delivery proof - into the repository under the NPN.
Apply the retention label of 5 years after termination so the record outlives any complaint window.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, co-code, state, event type and transmission date.
Give Market Conduct the index reference for the appointment data call pack.
checklist.done: every case folder is filed under the NPN, labelled for 5-year retention and searchable by state and event type.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination events
actions: Extract every executed producer agreement, every first application by a previously unappointed NPN, and every separation, resignation and for-cause action in the quarter.
Extract the HRIS leaver feed and the SIU action log independently and add any event the licensing register does not already hold.
Reconcile the event count to the register and treat any event present in a source feed but absent from the register as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction date and the queries used.
testing.done: the event population is reconciled to contracting, new business, HRIS and SIU sources and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the NIPR appointment record
actions: Pull the company's full PDB appointment extract by co-code and state as at quarter end.
Match every register appointment row to a live PDB appointment and every termination row to a PDB termination with the same effective date.
List appointments PDB shows that the register does not, and terminations the register shows that PDB does not.
Treat a register row with no PDB counterpart as a filing that never happened, regardless of what the case notes say.
testing.done: every register row is matched to PDB or listed as an unmatched break.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to the risky events
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of events in states whose window is shorter than 15 days.
Take 30 remaining events at random with a recorded seed, split between appointments and terminations.
Force in every event the register already flagged Late so the late-handling path is tested too.
Record the seed, strata, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all for-cause terminations, all short-window states and all flagged late events.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory day count for every sampled event
actions: Read the sampled state's statute or bulletin directly and record the window and whether it counts calendar or business days.
Recompute deadline = trigger or termination effective date + window, and elapsed = transmission date - trigger date.
Compare your recomputation to the register's deadline and Late flag; a wrong window in the per-state table is a systemic finding, not a single exception.
Capture the statute page relied on into the workpaper with the date read.
testing.done: every sampled event has an independently recomputed deadline and elapsed day count with a captured statutory source.

testing.step: Re-perform the NIPR lookup and confirm the transaction is real
actions: Search the recorded NIPR confirmation number and open the transaction detail for each sampled event.
Confirm the co-code, NPN, state, lines and effective date on the transaction match the register row exactly.
Read the transaction status and reject any case closed on a submission that later rejected and was never re-transmitted.
Capture the transaction detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled event traces to a completed NIPR transaction whose details match the register row.

testing.step: Test the for-cause package end to end
actions: For each for-cause termination read the filed statement against the investigation file and confirm every asserted fact is evidenced.
Confirm a dated counsel approval pre-dates transmission and that the statement went to the state by the channel the statute names.
Recompute the producer notice date as Commissioner notification date plus 15 days and confirm the delivery proof falls inside it.
Treat a for-cause termination reported as not for cause as a reportable failure, since the state loses the conduct information entirely.
testing.done: every for-cause package shows an evidenced statement, dated counsel approval and a timely, proven producer notice.

testing.step: Test the just-in-time states against actual first policy issues
actions: Extract every first policy issued in a JIT state for an NPN with no prior appointment in that state during the quarter.
Match each to an appointment transmitted inside the state's post-issue window.
Confirm the producer held an active licence on the application signed date even where the appointment followed the issue.
List issues with no follow-on appointment as fails and quantify the premium involved.
testing.done: every JIT first issue is matched to a timely follow-on appointment and a licence active at the signed date.

testing.step: Prove the post-termination shut-off actually took effect
actions: For each sampled termination query new business submissions and commission payments under the NPN after the termination effective date.
Pull the identity platform's access-revocation record for the agent portal and confirm the revocation date matches the effective date.
Trace 5 orphaned books to a receiving producer licensed and appointed in the same state and line.
List any post-termination submission or commission payment with its amount and the reason it was allowed.
testing.done: no sampled NPN shows post-termination submissions, payments or live access, or each occurrence is quantified and explained.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, state, event type, days late and any state late-filing penalty exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: trigger never raised, wrong window in the table, NIPR reject not reworked, for-cause misclassified, producer notice missed, or shut-off not applied.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and where a filing was never made, transmit it immediately and record the voluntary late-filing explanation to the state.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, for missed filings, a completed catch-up transmission.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Compute the late-filing rate against the 3% threshold and count missed for-cause notices and never-filed terminations against the zero threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who transmitted and approved none of the sampled events, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the results and any never-filed termination to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with the late-filing rate, the zero-threshold counts, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.
