checklist.step: Build the renewal calendar from the PDB expiration dates
actions: Run a PDB bulk extract for every appointed NPN and read the resident and non-resident licence expiration dates.

Load the expiry dates into the renewal calendar keyed on NPN, resident state and licence class, and mark the cycle length the state uses (biennial for Alabama, Arkansas and California; a 4-year cycle for Arizona).
Group producers into monthly cohorts by expiry month - for Alabama that is the last day of the licensee's birth month, so the cohort follows birthdays rather than a fixed date.
Reconcile the calendar count to the appointed producer roster and investigate any appointed NPN with no expiry date rather than dropping it.
checklist.done: every appointed NPN sits in a dated expiry cohort with its cycle length, reconciled to the appointed roster.

checklist.step: Look up each producer's CE requirement from their resident state
actions: For each cohort read the resident state's CE page and record total hours, ethics hours, classroom-versus-self-study limits, carry-over rules and the CE completion deadline relative to expiry.
Record the representative case explicitly: Alabama requires 24 hours per biennial renewal including 3 hours of ethics for a major-lines producer, with reduced hours for limited-lines classes.
Note the states that require CE only of resident licensees and grant non-resident CE reciprocity, so a producer is not chased for hours they do not owe.
Date-stamp each state entry in the CE requirement table with the page you read and the date read.
checklist.done: each producer's required hours, ethics hours and CE deadline are recorded from a dated read of their resident state's CE page.

checklist.step: Pull the state CE transcript for every producer in the cohort
actions: Pull the CE transcript status available through PDB and, where the state maintains its own CE transcript service, pull the state transcript for the same NPN.
Read banked hours by category - general, ethics, annuity, long-term care, flood - and the credit dates, since only hours banked inside the current cycle count.
Never accept a producer's own statement of hours as evidence; the state transcript is the record the department will examine.
Attach the dated transcript to the producer's renewal case.
checklist.done: each cohort producer has a dated state CE transcript on the renewal case showing banked hours by category.

checklist.step: Compute the shortfall by category and rank it by urgency
actions: For each producer compute shortfall = required hours - banked hours, separately for total hours and for ethics hours.
Flag the ethics trap: a producer with 24 total hours but zero ethics hours is short, not compliant, in every state that ring-fences ethics.
Rank shortfalls by days to expiry and by hours outstanding so the desk works the ones that cannot recover first.
Publish the shortfall list to the Territory Manager and the Agency Relations Manager weekly for the cohorts inside 90 days.
checklist.done: every cohort producer has a computed total and ethics shortfall, ranked by days to expiry and published weekly.

checklist.step: Test the product-specific training clocks that run alongside CE
actions: For annuity writers confirm the one-time 4-hour annuity best interest training under the NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions model is complete, plus any state top-up course a state added when it adopted the 2020 revisions.
For long-term care writers confirm the 8-hour initial training and compute the 4-hour refresher due date as the last completion plus 24 months.
For flood writers confirm the 3-hour NFIP course required by the Flood Insurance Reform Act minimum training requirement.
Write each clock's next due date onto the producer record so it drives an assignment rather than being rediscovered at renewal.
checklist.done: annuity, LTC and flood training clocks each carry a next-due date on the producer record.

checklist.step: Assign the courses that close the shortfall
actions: Assign courses from the state-approved provider catalogue only, matching the state, the credit category and the hours needed - a course approved in one state does not automatically bank in another.
Set the due date at least 21 days before the state's CE deadline to allow provider reporting time to the state's CE tracking service.
Enrol the producer, send the assignment with the reason and the expiry date, and copy their field leader.
Record the provider number, course number and approved credit hours on the assignment so the completion can be traced on the state transcript.
checklist.done: every shortfall producer has state-approved course assignments with provider and course numbers and a due date 21 days before the CE deadline.

checklist.step: Run the escalation cadence to expiry
actions: Send the producer a notification at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-14 days to expiry stating hours outstanding, ethics hours outstanding and the exact expiry date.
Copy the Territory Manager from T-30 and the Head of Distribution from T-14, with the in-force premium the producer services so the business consequence is visible.
Log every contact with date, channel and response on the renewal case.
At T-14 with hours still outstanding, issue the written warning that appointments will be suspended on the expiry date.
checklist.done: each producer has a logged contact at every cadence point, with field leadership copied from T-30 and a written warning at T-14 where needed.

checklist.step: Confirm the completed hours actually banked at the state
actions: Re-pull the state CE transcript 7 days after each reported completion and confirm the hours appear with the right category and credit date.
Chase the education provider directly where a completion has not posted, since providers typically report to the state within 7 to 10 days and the producer cannot renew until it lands.
Escalate any course that banked in the wrong category - general hours posted against an ethics requirement will not satisfy the state.
Mark the renewal case CE-Complete only on the strength of the transcript, never on a course certificate alone.
checklist.done: every completion is confirmed on the state transcript in the correct category before the case is marked CE-Complete.

checklist.step: Transmit the renewal through NIPR and pay the fees
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Licence Renewal, select the state and enter the NPN for each CE-Complete producer in the cohort.
Answer the background and regulatory-action questions from the current screening record rather than copying last cycle's answers.
Pay the state renewal fee and the NIPR transaction fee and capture the confirmation number and date.
Re-pull PDB after processing and confirm the new expiration date, then update the renewal calendar with the next cycle.
checklist.done: each renewal shows a NIPR confirmation number and a PDB expiry date advanced to the next cycle.

checklist.step: Suspend writing rights the moment a licence lapses
actions: Run the daily NIPR alert file and identify any NPN whose status left Active at expiry.
Set the solicitation flag to Suspended with the effective date equal to the expiry date, so new business intake and quoting reject the NPN the same day.
Hold commission on any policy with an application signed date after the expiry date pending the licensing determination.
Notify the producer and the Territory Manager in writing the same day, stating that solicitation must stop immediately.
checklist.done: every lapsed NPN is suspended on the expiry date with commission held and written notice sent the same day.

checklist.step: Work the reinstatement window before it closes
actions: For each lapsed producer read the state's reinstatement terms - Alabama allows reinstatement within 12 months of expiry on payment of the renewal fee plus a penalty and completion of the outstanding CE, after which re-examination and a fresh application are required.
Compute and record the reinstatement deadline as expiry date plus the state's window and load it into the calendar.
Complete the outstanding CE first, confirm it on the transcript, then submit the reinstatement transaction and capture the confirmation.
Where the window will close unmet, tell the Head of Distribution in writing so the book can be reassigned rather than left orphaned.
checklist.done: each lapse has a computed reinstatement deadline and either a completed reinstatement or a written reassignment decision.

checklist.step: Evidence any claimed CE exemption rather than accepting it
actions: For every producer claiming an exemption identify the basis - long-service and age exemptions offered by some states, limited-lines classes with reduced hours, non-resident reciprocity, or a documented medical or military deferral.
Obtain the state's written confirmation or the statute and rule text granting the exemption and attach it to the producer record with the date read.
Re-test each exemption at every renewal, because reciprocity dies the moment the resident licence changes state or lapses.
Never leave a producer record showing only 'CE not required'.
checklist.done: every claimed exemption carries a named basis, a cited source and a re-test date at the next renewal.

checklist.step: Align appointments with the renewed licence position
actions: After each cohort renewal, compare the renewed lines of authority to the appointed lines on the PDB appointment record.
Terminate appointments for lines the producer no longer holds and file the terminations inside the state's window.
Restore the solicitation flag to Approved only after PDB shows the licence active and the appointment intact.
Update the per-state writing scope on the producer record to the renewed lines.
checklist.done: appointed lines equal renewed lines for every cohort producer and the writing scope reflects the renewed licence.

checklist.step: Publish the renewal and CE dashboard
actions: Build the dashboard on the renewal calendar and CE transcript feed showing, by state and by field leader, producers at T-90 / T-60 / T-30 / expired and their outstanding total and ethics hours.
Add the product-training panel showing annuity, LTC refresher and flood clocks due in the next 90 days.
Add a lapse panel showing suspended NPNs, days into the reinstatement window and any post-expiry business detected.
Distribute weekly to Distribution leadership and monthly to the Compliance Committee pack.
checklist.done: a weekly dashboard shows renewal ageing, CE shortfalls, training clocks and lapses by state and field leader.

checklist.step: File the CE and renewal evidence and apply retention
actions: Move each renewal case - CE transcripts, course certificates with provider and course numbers, exemption evidence, NIPR renewal confirmation and the PDB after-capture - into the repository under the producer NPN and cycle.
Apply the retention label of 5 years from the end of the cycle so the record covers the state's own CE audit look-back.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, resident state, cycle end date and CE completion status.
Hand the index reference to Market Conduct for the producer-licensing exam pack.
checklist.done: each renewal case is filed under NPN and cycle, labelled for 5-year retention and searchable by state and cycle end date.

testing.step: Build the population of the period's expiring and renewed licences
actions: Extract from PDB every appointed NPN whose licence expiry fell inside the test period, with resident state, class and lines.
Add every producer whose annuity or LTC training clock came due in the period from the learning management system.
Reconcile the extract to the appointed producer roster and investigate any appointed NPN absent from the PDB extract.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extraction date and query parameters.
testing.done: the expiring cohort reconciles to the appointed roster and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the renewal calendar to the regulator's expiry dates
actions: Match every calendar row to the PDB expiry date on NPN and state.
List every producer whose calendar date differs from PDB, since a wrong date means the whole reminder cadence fired against the wrong day.
Check the cohorting logic against the state rule - for Alabama confirm the cohort follows the last day of the birth month, not a fixed anniversary.
Treat any appointed producer missing from the calendar entirely as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the calendar is reconciled date by date to PDB and every difference or omission is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to near-miss renewals
actions: Take 100% of producers who lapsed, reinstated, or renewed within 5 days of expiry.
Take 30 routine renewals at random using a recorded seed, spread across at least 8 resident states.
Force in every producer claiming a CE exemption and every LTC refresher that came due in the period.
Record the seed, strata, population size and draw date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all lapses, near-miss renewals, exemptions and due LTC refreshers.

testing.step: Re-perform the CE requirement determination from the state's own page
actions: For each sampled producer open the resident state's CE requirements page and reach your own conclusion on total hours, ethics hours and the CE deadline before looking at the CE table.
Compare to the recorded requirement; for the representative case confirm Alabama's 24 hours including 3 ethics per biennial cycle was applied to a major-lines producer.
Treat a right hour count sourced from a stale table entry as an exception, because the next bulletin will break it.
Capture the CE page into the workpaper with the date read.
testing.done: every sampled requirement is independently re-derived from a captured, dated state CE page.

testing.step: Trace banked hours to the state transcript, not the internal record
actions: Pull the state CE transcript for each sampled NPN directly and total the hours credited inside the cycle by category.
Compare to the hours the renewal case claimed and to the certificates held internally.
Confirm each credited course shows an approved provider number for that state and a credit date inside the cycle.
List any renewal that relied on certificates never posted to the state transcript.
testing.done: banked hours per the state transcript agree with the renewal case for every sampled producer, or the difference is listed.

testing.step: Recompute the renewal and reinstatement day counts
actions: Recompute the CE deadline and the renewal date against the state's rule and compare to the actual completion and renewal dates.
For lapses recompute the reinstatement deadline as expiry plus the state's window - 12 months for Alabama - and confirm the reinstatement fell inside it.
Recompute the LTC refresher due date as last completion plus 24 months and confirm no LTC sale fell after it.
Flag every renewal where CE was banked after the state's own CE deadline even though the licence still renewed.
testing.done: every sampled date is independently recomputed and any late CE, late renewal or missed refresher is quantified in days.

testing.step: Test for business written on a lapsed or CE-deficient licence
actions: For every lapsed NPN query applications signed and policies bound between the expiry date and the reinstatement date.
For LTC and annuity writers query sales made after a training clock expired.
Quantify policy count, premium and commission paid for each hit and identify the state so the reporting obligation can be assessed.
Treat any hit as a breach for reporting, not as a test exception to be rated.
testing.done: post-lapse and post-training-expiry sales are quantified by policy count, premium and commission, or confirmed nil.

testing.step: Prove the suspension and reminder controls actually operated
actions: Pull the solicitation flag change history and confirm each lapsed NPN was suspended with an effective date equal to its expiry date.
Pull the notification log and confirm contacts exist at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-14 for each sampled producer, with the field leader copied from T-30.
Pull the commission hold report and confirm holds were placed on post-expiry business.
List every suspension applied late, with the number of days between expiry and suspension.
testing.done: flag history, notification log and commission holds each evidence the control operating, or the gaps are listed with day counts.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying NPN, resident state, cycle end date, hours short, days lapsed and any premium written during the lapse.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: wrong expiry date, stale CE requirement, hours never banked, ethics hours missed, cadence not run, suspension applied late, or exemption unevidenced.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for business written during a lapse agree the honour-and-clawback position with the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where business was written on a lapse, an agreed disposition.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Compute the renewal-miss rate against the 1% threshold and the count of policies written during a lapse against the zero threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references for each figure.
Have a reviewer outside Licensing Ops, who chased or filed none of the sampled renewals, sign the workpaper.
Report the results, all lapses and any post-lapse business to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with the renewal-miss rate, post-lapse policy count, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the 18 U.S.C. sec. 1033 prohibited-person determination for every new hire, contractor and producer engaged in the business of insurance, and owns the sec. 1033(e)(2) written consent file

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 18 U.S.C. sec. 1033(e)(1)(A) (no person convicted of a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, or a felony under sec. 1033, may engage in the business of insurance affecting interstate commerce without written consent) and sec. 1034 enforcement, read with Ala. Code sec. 27-7-19 licence denial grounds and the ALDOI consent-application instructions; Arkansas, Arizona and California consent procedures read from their own department pages

In-scope processes.value: Pre-engagement screening at offer or contract stage for employees, temporary staff, contractors, appointed producers and agency DRLPs whose duties touch underwriting, claims, sales, servicing, premium handling or the insurance data those functions rely on

In-scope systems.value: Screening triggered from the recruiting record at offer stage; vendor background results and the 1033 attestation stored against the person record with restricted access

Compliance procedure documented.value: 1033 Screening and Consent Procedure - trigger points, attestation wording, FCRA-compliant background order, fingerprint requirement by state, RIRS and sanctions searches, felony analysis, engagement block, consent application and adverse action steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Employment Counsel and Privacy Counsel concurrence; reviewed annually and on any change to state fingerprint or fair-chance hiring requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per hire - screening must clear before the start date or first solicitation; the FCRA pre-adverse notice must be followed by at least 5 business days before the final adverse action notice; state consent applications commonly take 60-90 days, so any conditional engagement is blocked for that whole period

Deadline reminders configured.value: Recruiting workflow alerts at day 3 and day 7 of an open screening, an automatic hold 5 days before any start date with screening incomplete, and calendar reminders for annual re-attestation on the hire anniversary

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed 1033 attestation, FCRA disclosure and authorisation, the consumer report, fingerprint results, RIRS and sanctions search evidence and any state consent order retained 7 years after the engagement ends, in a restricted-access folder

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person engaged in the business of insurance without a completed screening, and any prohibited person engaged without a sec. 1033(e)(2) written consent, is logged with the engagement dates, duties performed and the removal or consent-application decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every prohibited-person determination, every consent application and every decision to continue an engagement pending consent

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every employee, contractor and producer engaged in the business of insurance whose start date or contract effective date fell in the quarter, plus every existing person whose annual re-attestation came due

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - one prohibited person engaged without written consent, or one start date with no completed screening, is a fail; documentation-only defects tolerated to 2% of the sample

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per hire; the test runs quarterly over the quarter's engagements at 100% coverage of anyone with a disclosed criminal, regulatory or sanctions hit, plus an annual sweep of the whole population against RIRS

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside HR and Compliance Ops and must not have performed or adjudicated any sampled screening

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly 1033 screening test workpaper (engagement population, screening evidence references, adjudication re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository, with the underlying personal data referenced rather than copied

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening completion register, the attestation set and any state consent orders, producible to a market conduct or department inquiry within 10 business days without disclosing raw consumer reports

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Officer answers department inquiries about a specific individual; General Counsel clears any disclosure of criminal history and any admission that a prohibited person was engaged

checklist.step: Trigger screening at offer or contract stage, before any start date is confirmed
actions: On moving a candidate to Offer, set the screening requirement flag on the requisition based on the role's function - underwriting, claims, sales, servicing, premium handling or supporting data access all count as the business of insurance.
For producers and agencies, take the same trigger from the contracting workflow at agreement issue rather than at appointment.
Record the intended start date or contract effective date on the screening case so the block can be enforced against it.
Never issue a start date confirmation before the screening case is opened.
checklist.done: every offer and producer agreement has an open screening case carrying the role's in-scope determination and the intended start date.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed 1033 attestation and the FCRA disclosure and authorisation
actions: Send the candidate the 1033 attestation asking, in the statute's own terms, whether they have been convicted of any felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust or any felony under 18 U.S.C. sec. 1033, in any jurisdiction, at any time.
Send the FCRA standalone disclosure and written authorisation as separate documents from the application, since bundling them defeats the disclosure.
Add the state-specific notices the candidate's work location requires and the summary of rights under the FCRA.
File the executed documents against the person record with restricted access and record the signature date on the case.
checklist.done: a signed 1033 attestation, a standalone FCRA disclosure and a written authorisation are on file with their signature dates.

checklist.step: Order the background check from the screening vendor
actions: Order the package the role requires: county and federal criminal search covering the last 7 years and every jurisdiction of residence, national criminal database, sex offender registry, and - only where the role handles premium or company funds and the state permits it - a credit check.
Set the scope to report convictions rather than arrests, and to comply with the fair-chance and ban-the-box limits of the work location.
Record the vendor order number and order date on the screening case and chase anything open beyond 7 days.
Route any report with a hit straight to Compliance without circulating it to the hiring manager.
checklist.done: the ordered package matches the role and jurisdiction, with the vendor order number and date recorded and hits routed to Compliance only.

checklist.step: Order fingerprints where the state or the licence class requires them
actions: Read the resident state's producer licensing page for its fingerprint requirement and its designated vendor and service code.
Schedule the candidate through the state's fingerprint vendor and record the transaction control number and capture date.
Confirm the state received the criminal history response, since a licence application will sit pending until it lands.
Log the fingerprint result reference on the screening case without copying the underlying criminal history into the HR file.
checklist.done: fingerprints are captured through the state's designated vendor with a recorded control number and a confirmed state response.

checklist.step: Search the regulatory action and licence history record
actions: For anyone who holds or has held an insurance licence, run a PDB report by NPN and read the Regulatory Actions section sourced from the NAIC Regulatory Information Retrieval System.
Record every action with state, date, type and underlying conduct, and order the consent order or state order for any action involving misappropriation, forgery, rebating or unlicensed activity.
Check for surrendered or revoked licences in other states, which frequently precede a 1033 issue.
Attach the dated PDB report to the screening case.
checklist.done: a dated PDB regulatory-action review is on the case for every licensed or previously licensed person.

checklist.step: Run sanctions and exclusion screening on the same person
actions: Screen the full legal name, any known aliases and the date of birth against OFAC SDN and consolidated lists, and against the applicable denied-party and exclusion lists.
Adjudicate every hit to a documented true or false positive with the identifiers you relied on - do not clear a hit on name alone.
Escalate any true positive to the Financial Crime AML Officer and the Compliance Officer immediately and hold the engagement.
Record the screening date, list versions and disposition on the case.
checklist.done: the person is screened against current sanctions and exclusion lists with every hit adjudicated and dated.

checklist.step: Analyse any conviction against the section 1033 test
actions: For each reported conviction establish the offence, jurisdiction, felony or misdemeanour classification and disposition date from the court record, not the vendor summary.

Apply the statutory test: is it a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, or any felony under 18 U.S.C. sec. 1033 - noting that theft, fraud, forgery, embezzlement, perjury and money laundering typically qualify while many other felonies do not.
Treat expungements, pardons and deferred adjudications carefully and take the position the state department takes rather than the candidate's.
Write the determination - prohibited person or not - with the reasoning and the source documents onto the case, and sign and date it.
checklist.done: every conviction has a written, dated counsel determination against the statutory test citing the court record relied on.

checklist.step: Block the engagement where a prohibited person is identified
actions: Set the screening case to Prohibited - Blocked and notify HR and the hiring manager that the start date cannot proceed, without disclosing the underlying conviction detail.
For a producer, hold the appointment transmission and keep the solicitation flag unset.
Record that a prohibited person may not participate in the business of insurance in any capacity, including unpaid or advisory roles, until written consent is granted.
Notify General Counsel the same day and agree whether a consent application will be supported.
checklist.done: the engagement is blocked, HR and the manager are notified without conviction detail, and General Counsel has the case.

checklist.step: Prepare and submit the section 1033(e)(2) written consent application
actions: Identify the correct granting authority - the insurance regulator of the state in which the person will engage in the business of insurance - and read that department's consent-application instructions.

Assemble the packet: the application form, certified court records showing the offence and its disposition, evidence of rehabilitation, references, the proposed role description and the company's supervision plan.
Submit through the department's stated channel, capture the submission receipt and record the department's expected turnaround, commonly 60 to 90 days.
Track the department's response and file the granted consent - noting it is role and state specific, so a change of duties or state may require a fresh consent.
checklist.done: a complete consent application is submitted with a captured receipt and the response is tracked to a written grant or denial.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA adverse action sequence where the report drives the decision
actions: Send the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the FCRA summary of rights, and record the send date.
Wait at least 5 business days for the candidate to dispute or explain, and log any response and its handling.

Where the decision stands, send the final adverse action notice naming the consumer reporting agency, stating it did not make the decision, and setting out the right to a free file disclosure and to dispute.
File both notices and the delivery evidence on the screening case.
checklist.done: pre-adverse and final notices are on file with at least 5 business days between them and any candidate response logged.

checklist.step: Release the screening result to Licensing before any appointment
actions: Read the screening disposition - Cleared, Blocked, or Cleared subject to consent - from the case rather than from an email.
Record the disposition and its date on the producer record and release the appointment only on Cleared, or on Cleared subject to consent once the consent order is on file.
Answer the NIPR licence and renewal background questions consistently with the screening record.
Where a disposition changes later, suspend the solicitation flag the same day.
checklist.done: no appointment is transmitted without a Cleared disposition dated earlier than the transmission.

checklist.step: Re-attest the existing population annually
actions: Issue the annual 1033 re-attestation to every employee and appointed producer in scope, asking about convictions since the last attestation and any pending charges.
Set a 30-day completion window and escalate non-responders to their manager or field leader at day 20.
Route every positive response to Regulatory Counsel within one business day for a fresh determination.
Record completion rates by business unit for the Compliance Committee pack.
checklist.done: the annual re-attestation is issued to the full in-scope population with a tracked completion rate and every positive response adjudicated.

checklist.step: Monitor continuously for post-hire regulatory and criminal events
actions: Subscribe every appointed NPN to the NIPR alert feed for new regulatory actions and licence status changes and work the daily file.
Run the sanctions and exclusion rescreen on the in-scope population at the frequency the financial crime policy sets.
Require self-reporting of any arrest or charge within 5 business days as a condition of the producer agreement and the employee code of conduct, and act on each report.
Open a fresh screening case on any hit rather than amending the original.
checklist.done: daily alerts, periodic rescreening and a self-reporting duty are all operating with each hit opening a new case.

checklist.step: Enforce the engagement block in the systems that grant access
actions: Make the joiner provisioning workflow read the screening disposition and refuse to create accounts for a Blocked case.
Set the leaver and status-change workflow to revoke access the same day a disposition moves to Blocked.
Run a monthly recertification comparing active accounts in policy, claims and agent systems to Cleared dispositions.
Report any account found without a Cleared disposition to the Compliance Officer within one business day.
checklist.done: provisioning is gated on a Cleared disposition and the monthly recertification finds no active account without one.

checklist.step: File the screening evidence under restricted access and apply retention
actions: Move the screening case - attestation, FCRA documents, vendor report reference, fingerprint reference, PDB and sanctions evidence, counsel determination, consent order - into a restricted-access folder keyed on person id.
Apply the retention label of 7 years after the engagement ends and set access to Compliance, Employment Counsel and the named auditors only.
Confirm the repository logs every access to the folder, because these are criminal-history and consumer-report records.
Publish only the screening completion register, not the underlying reports, to the wider compliance evidence set.
checklist.done: the case is filed under restricted access with a 7-year label, access logging on, and only the completion register published more widely.

testing.step: Build the population of people engaged in the business of insurance
actions: Extract every employee and worker with a start date in the quarter, with job family, work location and business unit.
Add contractors and temporary staff from the vendor management and contingent worker records, and producers and DRLPs newly contracted in the quarter.
Apply the in-scope test by function and list anyone excluded with the reason, so the scoping judgement itself is testable.
Reconcile the count to payroll starters and to the contracting log and clear the difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population covers employees, contingent workers and producers, reconciles to payroll and contracting, and records every scoping exclusion.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to completed screening cases
actions: Match every population row to a screening case on person id or NPN.
Compare the screening completion date to the start or contract effective date and list every case completed after engagement began.
List every person with no screening case at all as an automatic exception regardless of role seniority.
Check that each case's in-scope determination matches the role's actual duties as described in the job record.
testing.done: every person is matched to a screening case completed before engagement, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to disclosed hits
actions: Take 100% of cases with a criminal, regulatory or sanctions hit, and 100% of prohibited-person determinations and consent applications.
Take 30 clean cases at random using a recorded seed, spread across employees, contingent workers and producers.
Force in every case where the start date preceded the screening completion date.
Record the seed, strata, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all hits, all determinations and all late-completed screenings.

testing.step: Re-perform the section 1033 adjudication independently
actions: For each sampled hit read the underlying court record and reach your own conclusion on whether the offence is a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust or a felony under sec. 1033.
Compare to the recorded determination without reading it first; a correct conclusion reasoned from the vendor summary rather than the court record is still an exception.
Check the treatment of expungements, pardons and deferred adjudications against the position the relevant department takes.
Capture the citation and the court record reference into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled hit has an independent, sourced adjudication note compared to the recorded determination.

testing.step: Test the consent position for every prohibited person
actions: For each prohibited person confirm either that the engagement never began, or that a written sec. 1033(e)(2) consent from the correct state authority pre-dates the first day of work.
Read the consent order and confirm it covers the actual role and state the person works in, since consents are role and jurisdiction specific.
Confirm the supervision conditions the consent imposes are operating and evidenced.
Treat any engagement running on a pending application as a breach, not a timing difference.
testing.done: every prohibited person is either not engaged or covered by a pre-dating, role-matched consent with its conditions evidenced.

testing.step: Test the FCRA process on every adverse decision in the sample
actions: Confirm the disclosure was a standalone document and the authorisation was signed before the report was ordered.
Confirm a pre-adverse notice with the report and the summary of rights was sent, and recompute the interval to the final notice as at least 5 business days.
Confirm the final notice names the consumer reporting agency and states the agency did not make the decision.
List any decision taken with no pre-adverse notice as a fail.
testing.done: every adverse decision shows a compliant disclosure, a pre-adverse notice and a final notice at least 5 business days apart.

testing.step: Test the regulatory and sanctions searches actually ran
actions: Re-run the PDB report for each sampled licensed person and compare the regulatory actions found today to those recorded at screening.
Re-run sanctions and exclusion screening on the sampled names and compare hits and dispositions.
Confirm each recorded hit disposition names the identifiers relied on rather than clearing on name alone.
List any regulatory action that existed at screening date but was never recorded.
testing.done: PDB and sanctions searches are independently re-run and every pre-existing action or hit was captured at screening.

testing.step: Prove access was never granted ahead of a Cleared disposition
actions: Pull account creation dates for each sampled person in the policy administration, claims and agent portal systems.
Compare each creation date to the screening completion date and the disposition.
Pull the monthly recertification results and list any active account held by a Blocked or unscreened person.
Screenshot the provisioning gate rejecting a test identity with no Cleared disposition.
testing.done: no sampled account pre-dates its Cleared disposition and the provisioning gate rejection is captured.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying person id or NPN, role, engagement date, screening gap and, where applicable, the duties performed while unscreened.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: trigger missed, scoping wrong, report ordered late, adjudication unsourced, consent not obtained, adverse action mishandled, or access provisioned early.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any prohibited person engaged without consent agree removal from insurance duties and a self-report position with General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, for prohibited persons, a removal and self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Count prohibited persons engaged without consent and start dates with no completed screening against the zero threshold, and compute the documentation defect rate against the 2% threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references, and keep personal data out of the narrative.
Have the Internal Auditor, who performed and adjudicated none of the sampled screenings, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with both threshold counts, a stated conclusion, no personal data in the narrative, and a committee reporting date.

Code sec. 27-7-30 (an insurer must appoint each producer who represents it) and sec. 27-7-31 (commission may be paid only to a licensed and appointed producer), read with the ALDOI appointment renewal instructions each quarter; Arkansas, Arizona and California appointment and commission-payment statutes checked from their own department pages

In-scope systems.value: Internal roster and writing-scope record matched against the NIPR PDB appointment extract and the commission ledger; the reconciliation pack held in the compliance evidence repository

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly - the roster freezes at quarter end, the PDB extract is ordered within 5 business days, the match runs within 10 business days and every break is cleared within 30 days of quarter end; stale appointments must be terminated before each state's annual appointment renewal invoice date

checklist.step: Freeze the internal producer roster at quarter end
actions: Extract as at the last calendar day of the quarter every producer record with NPN, entity NPN, writing company co-code, states, lines, solicitation flag and contract status.
Take the extract as a point-in-time snapshot with a row count and file hash so it cannot drift while the reconciliation runs.
Include terminated producers whose termination effective date falls inside the quarter, because their appointments should have been ended too.
Publish the frozen file to the reconciliation folder and notify the Producer Licensing Coordinator that the extract is available.
checklist.done: a hashed, row-counted roster snapshot as at quarter end is in the reconciliation folder with terminated producers included.

checklist.step: Order the NIPR appointment extract for every writing company and state
actions: In NIPR Gateway order the appointment report for each co-code covering every state the company is authorised in, within 5 business days of quarter end.
Request the file in the delimited format that carries NPN, state, appointment effective date, appointment status, lines appointed and termination date.
Confirm the returned row count against the state count expected, since a missing state file silently hides every break in that state.
Save the file dated and hashed alongside the roster snapshot.
checklist.done: a dated, hashed NIPR appointment extract covering every co-code and authorised state is in the reconciliation folder.

checklist.step: Pull the commission ledger for the quarter
actions: Extract every commission payment settled in the quarter with writing NPN, payee entity, policy number, state, product, transaction date and amount.
Include advances, bonuses and overrides, since a payment to an unappointed producer is a payment whatever it is called.
Reconcile the extract total to the commission expense posted in the general ledger for the quarter and clear the difference before the match runs.
Save the extract with a row count and hash into the reconciliation folder.
checklist.done: a hashed commission extract covering advances, bonuses and overrides is reconciled to the general ledger commission expense.

checklist.step: Normalise the keys before matching anything
actions: Load the three extracts into the reconciliation schema and standardise NPN to the 1-10 digit numeric form, stripping leading zeros and stray characters.
Standardise state to the two-letter USPS code and co-code to the five-digit NAIC form.
Report every row that fails key standardisation as a data-quality break rather than dropping it - a null NPN is exactly where an unappointed producer hides.
Publish row counts before and after normalisation so nothing disappears silently.
checklist.done: all three extracts share standardised NPN, state and co-code keys, with before-and-after row counts published and no rows dropped.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match
actions: Join roster to NIPR appointments on NPN + co-code + state and mark matched, roster-only or NIPR-only.
Join the commission extract on writing NPN + co-code + state and mark whether an active appointment existed on the transaction date, not merely at quarter end.
Produce one output row per NPN-co-code-state combination carrying all three statuses and the commission amount.
Reconcile the output row count to the union of the three inputs so the match itself is provably complete.
checklist.done: a single match output exists per NPN-co-code-state with all three statuses, reconciled to the union of the inputs.

checklist.step: Type every break so it can be routed
actions: Assign each break a type: Appointed-not-on-roster (over-appointment), On-roster-not-appointed (writing exposure), Commission-without-appointment, Terminated-but-still-appointed, Line-mismatch, or Key-quality.
Rank by risk - Commission-without-appointment and On-roster-not-appointed first, since both carry statutory exposure.
Attach to each break the supporting evidence: the roster row, the NIPR row and any commission rows, with amounts.
Route each type to its named owner with a 30-day clearance date from quarter end.
checklist.done: every break carries a type, a risk rank, its supporting rows and a named owner with a 30-day clearance date.

checklist.step: Investigate over-appointments and terminate the stale ones
actions: For each Appointed-not-on-roster break check whether the producer was ever contracted, has since terminated, or simply never had the roster record created.
Where the relationship genuinely ended, transmit the termination through NIPR with the correct effective date and reason, and confirm it on PDB.
Where the relationship exists but the roster record is missing, create the roster record with the correct scope rather than terminating a live appointment.
Complete all terminations before the state's appointment renewal invoice date so the company stops paying to appoint people it does not use.
checklist.done: every over-appointment is either terminated on PDB or explained by a corrected roster record, before the renewal invoice date.

checklist.step: Investigate producers writing without an appointment
actions: For each On-roster-not-appointed break query applications and policies written under that NPN in that state during the quarter and quantify count and premium.
Establish whether the state is a just-in-time appointment state and whether the post-issue window was still open.
Where business was written outside any permitted window, transmit the appointment immediately, note the days late, and refer the matter for a self-report assessment.
Where no business was written, correct the roster scope so the producer cannot solicit in that state until appointed.
checklist.done: every writing-without-appointment break is quantified in policies and premium and has either a corrective appointment or a closed writing scope.

checklist.step: Investigate commission paid without an appointment in force
actions: For each Commission-without-appointment break confirm the appointment status on the transaction date from the NIPR extract, not the quarter-end position.
Total the amount paid by NPN, state and payment type, separating renewal commission on pre-existing business from new business commission.

Refer the clawback decision to the Producer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel, since some states permit renewal commission to a formerly appointed producer while forbidding new business commission.
Where clawback is decided, raise the recovery against the payee account and track it to recovery or write-off.
checklist.done: every commission-without-appointment break is quantified by payment type with a documented clawback or permitted-payment decision.

checklist.step: Resolve line-of-authority mismatches between the roster and the appointment
actions: For each Line-mismatch break compare the lines on the internal writing scope, the lines appointed on NIPR and the lines licensed on PDB.
Where the internal scope is wider than the appointment, narrow the scope the same day and file the additional appointment lines if the business needs them.
Where the appointment is wider than the licence, terminate the excess lines, because an appointment cannot exceed what the licence grants.
Re-run the affected rows through the match to confirm the break clears.
checklist.done: internal scope, appointed lines and licensed lines agree for every mismatched row and the break clears on re-run.

checklist.step: Escalate anything with statutory exposure the same week
actions: Escalate to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel every break involving business written or commission paid without an appointment, within 5 business days of the match being published.
Present the exposure in writing: state, producer, policy count, premium, commission and the state's penalty regime.
Agree the self-report position per state and record the decision and its rationale.
Track each escalated item on the compliance issue register until the state has responded or the item is formally closed.
checklist.done: every statutory-exposure break has a written escalation, an agreed self-report position and an open register entry.

checklist.step: Reconcile the appointment renewal invoice to the cleared roster
actions: When each state's annual appointment renewal invoice arrives, compare the billed appointment count by co-code and state to the cleared roster count.
Query any billed appointment that the reconciliation shows as terminated and confirm the termination reached the state before the billing cut-off.
Post the invoice only for appointments the company intends to keep, and record the saving from terminated stale appointments.
Feed unexpected variances back to the Producer Licensing Coordinator as a new break.
checklist.done: each state's renewal invoice count reconciles to the cleared roster and every variance is raised as a break.

checklist.step: Publish the reconciliation report with break ageing
actions: Publish, within 10 business days of quarter end, a report showing match rate, break counts by type, exposure amounts and ageing buckets of 0-30, 31-60 and 60-plus days.
Break the view down by writing company, state and field leader so ownership is unambiguous.
Show the movement from the prior quarter and highlight any break carried forward for a second quarter.
Distribute to Distribution leadership, the Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee pack.
checklist.done: the report is published within 10 business days showing match rate, typed breaks, exposure and ageing by company, state and field leader.

checklist.step: Track every break to closure and re-run the match
actions: Open a GRC issue for every break not cleared within 30 days of quarter end, with owner, action and due date.
Re-run the match on the cleared rows and require the break to disappear from the output before the issue is closed - a closure note is not evidence.
Report any break aged beyond 60 days to the Head of Compliance individually.
Carry all open breaks into the next quarter's opening position so nothing resets at quarter end.
checklist.done: every uncleared break has a GRC issue and every closure is evidenced by the break disappearing from a re-run match.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation pack and apply retention
actions: Assemble the pack: the three hashed source extracts, the normalisation log, the match output, the break register with evidence, the corrective NIPR confirmations and the sign-off.
File it under the quarter and apply the retention label of 5 years from the reconciliation date.
Confirm the pack is searchable by quarter, co-code, state and break type.
Give Market Conduct the index reference so it can be handed to an appointment data call without rebuilding it.
checklist.done: the pack is filed under the quarter, labelled for 5-year retention and searchable by co-code, state and break type.

testing.step: Rebuild the population from source rather than accepting the extracts
actions: Re-extract the producer roster as at the same quarter-end date using the auditor's own query and compare the row count and hash to the frozen file.
Re-extract commission payments for the quarter and reconcile the total to the general ledger commission expense independently.
Confirm the reconciliation scope covered every writing company co-code and every state each is authorised in, using the CoA authority matrix as the completeness benchmark.
List any co-code or state absent from the reconciliation as a scope exception.
testing.done: the auditor's own extracts agree to the frozen files and the scope covers every co-code and authorised state.

testing.step: Reconcile the NIPR extract to the regulator's live record
actions: Order an independent PDB appointment extract for the same co-codes and states and compare row counts to the file used in the match.
Spot-check 20 appointment rows directly on the PDB screen for effective date, status and lines.
List any state whose file was missing or truncated in the original extract, since that hides every break in that state.
Capture the extract order confirmation and the spot-check screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: the NIPR file used in the match is confirmed complete against an independent extract and 20 direct PDB checks.

testing.step: Re-perform the three-way match independently
actions: Rebuild the join on NPN + co-code + state from the auditor's own extracts without reusing the team's query.
Compare your break count and break list to the published one and investigate every difference in both directions.
Test the key normalisation by re-running the match with raw keys and quantifying how many rows only match after standardisation.
List any row the original match dropped at normalisation.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt match reconciles to the published break list, with every difference and dropped row explained.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of breaks and matched rows
actions: Take 100% of On-roster-not-appointed and Commission-without-appointment breaks.
Take 25 other breaks at random with a recorded seed, spread across the remaining break types.
Take 25 rows the match reported as clean, to test for false negatives rather than only auditing the exceptions.
Record the seed, strata, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all statutory-exposure breaks and includes clean rows to test for false negatives.

testing.step: Re-perform the appointment status test as at the transaction date
actions: For each sampled commission payment read the PDB appointment history and establish the appointment status on the payment transaction date, not at quarter end.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the payment was permissible in that state before reading the team's disposition.
Check the renewal-versus-new-business distinction against the state's own rule, since the two are treated differently in several states.
Capture the PDB appointment history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled payment has an independent as-at-transaction-date permissibility conclusion with a captured PDB screen.

testing.step: Trace writing-without-appointment breaks to actual policies
actions: For each sampled break query policies bound under the NPN in that state during the quarter and total count and written premium.
Confirm whether the state operates just-in-time appointment and recompute whether the post-issue window was still open on the bind date.
Confirm any corrective appointment transmitted afterwards shows on PDB with its effective date and recompute the days late.
List any break closed as 'no business written' where policies in fact exist.
testing.done: each sampled break is traced to a policy count and premium, with the JIT window and corrective filing recomputed in days.

testing.step: Recompute the clearance clocks and the invoice reconciliation
actions: Recompute the freeze, extract, publish and clearance dates against the day 1 / day 5 / day 10 / day 30 standard and list every missed milestone.
Recompute break ageing from quarter end and list every break over 60 days.
Re-perform one state's appointment renewal invoice reconciliation from the invoice to the cleared roster count.
Quantify the fees paid to renew appointments that the reconciliation had already identified as stale.
testing.done: every milestone and ageing figure is recomputed and one invoice reconciliation is re-performed with stale-appointment fees quantified.

testing.step: Test that closures were evidenced by a re-run, not a note
actions: Pull the GRC issues raised for the quarter's breaks and read the closure evidence attached to each.
Confirm each closed break is genuinely absent from the latest match output rather than closed on an assertion.
List any issue closed with no attached evidence and any break that reappeared in the following quarter.
Confirm all open breaks were carried into the next quarter's opening position.
testing.done: every closed issue is supported by absence from a re-run match, and reappearing or uncarried breaks are listed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying co-code, state, NPN, break type, policy count, premium and commission at risk.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: scope incomplete, extract truncated, key normalisation dropped rows, break mis-typed, clearance missed, closure unevidenced, or corrective filing never transmitted.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and agree the self-report and clawback positions with Regulatory Counsel for statutory-exposure items.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where exposure exists, an agreed self-report and clawback position.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report it
actions: Compute the unmatched-roster rate against the 1% threshold, the count of production and commission attributable to unappointed producers against the zero threshold, and the count of breaks aged beyond 60 days.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who neither prepared the extracts nor cleared any sampled break, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion, the exposure amounts and any self-report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with the unmatched rate, exposure counts, ageing breaches, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.
